response.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_rental_duration) AS avg_rental_duration, AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_rate_to_cost_ratio FROM (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_duration) AS avg_rental_duration, AVG(CAST(rental_rate AS DOUBLE) / replacement_cost) AS avg_ratio FROM film WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99 GROUP BY rating) AS per_rating

assumptions.assumption: The filter is strict: only films with replacement_cost > 20.99 are included, so films at exactly 20.99 are excluded.
The outer result is an unweighted mean of the per-rating averages, so each rating counts equally regardless of how many films it has after filtering.

The ratio is computed per film as rental_rate / replacement_cost and then averaged within each rating. CAST to DOUBLE avoids MySQL's decimal division, which would truncate the ratio to about 4 decimal places and break the 'unrounded' requirement.

Missing values are ignored by AVG. The columns used are all NOT NULL in the schema, so this changes nothing here. The rating column is nullable, but the verified data shows only the five non-null levels.
The database is MySQL-compatible (the schema uses MySQL types such as TINYINT UNSIGNED, YEAR and BOOLEAN). The CAST(... AS DOUBLE) syntax depends on that dialect, and the schema does not confirm it.
